text:
tara (support): forwarding a billing escalation from ryan — invoice INV-1192 shows ~7.8k tokens but their SDK estimator reported ~5.2k. customer wants a quick reconciliation. payload and repro below.

ryan (customer): Hi, I ran a single request through your JS SDK and the estimator printed 5.2k tokens, but the invoice line item shows 7.8k. Attaching the request we used. Any chance something on your side injected extra tokens?

tara (support): thanks. ryan included both the curl and the SDK snippet. past issues were system message injection or hidden tool outputs, but we need to repro.

ryan (customer): CURL I used:
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-3b","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the following doc..."}],"stream":false}'
```

ryan (customer): JS SDK snippet (node):
```
const res = await Redwood.chat.create({
  model: 'redwood-3b',
  messages: [
    { role: 'system', content: 'You are a helpful assistant.' },
    { role: 'user', content: docText }
  ]
});
console.log(res.estimatedTokens); // 5200
console.log(res.outputText.length);
```

nate (eng): can someone paste the raw request id / metering ids from the invoice? need trace id to pull server side metering logs.

ryan (customer): invoice metadata: trace_id=tr-8a3c, request_id=req-20260312-771, charged_tokens=7802. I also have the server response body if helpful.

evan (infra): grabbing logs for req-20260312-771... got it. Server metering snapshot:
```
request_id: req-20260312-771
received_tokens: 5238
system_injected_tokens: 1540
tool_invocations: 1024
total_charged: 7802
```

billing-bot: note: invoice line items are computed from charged_tokens (total_charged) in metering snapshots.

nate (eng): ah — looks like two contributors: a system_injected block and a tool output. ryan's SDK estimator only counted the messages he passed (user + system) but not the server-side injected system content or tool responses. Is that expected?

tara (support): ryan — did you have any tool/function calls enabled in your request or any server-side plugins?

ryan (customer): we didn't intentionally call any tools. We just sent the doc. The SDK shows estimatedTokens for our messages only.

nate (eng): possible root cause: Model routing policy triggered an auxiliary tool (internal 'document-summarizer' plugin) on the server because of heuristic that doc exceeded cutoff. That plugin returned a structured summary which was concatenated into the assistant response before finalizing; those tokens are billed but the client SDK estimator never saw them. Additionally, runtime prepended a short system instruction (~1.5k tokens) to help model with formatting.

evan (infra): repro steps I used to validate: replayed req-20260312-771 against staging with metering debug flags enabled. Confirmed two injections: a 1540-token formatter system message and a 1024-token tool output. Repro commands:
```
# replay with metering debug
redwoodctl replay --request req-20260312-771 --debug-metering
```

nate (eng): quick mitigation: we can make SDKs surface an optional header X-EXPECTED-INJECTS to show estimated server-side injections (best-effort) OR add a new SDK flag include_server_injected=true that asks the control plane to return a metering_preview in the response. For now, tell ryan this billing looks correct given server-side injections.

ryan (customer): thanks. two questions: 1) why didn't the SDK warn us about possible tool calls? 2) is there a way to opt out of server-side plugins to avoid surprise tokens?

tara (support): answering: 1) current SDK estimator only tokenizes client-sent messages and local tool calls; it doesn't predict server-injected system/tool responses. 2) yes — you can set policy: { allow_server_plugins: false } in request metadata to opt out. I'll share a safe example.

tara (support): opt-out example (curl):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-3b","messages":[...],"metadata":{"allow_server_plugins":false}}'
```

evan (infra): follow-up note: we should add a meter-preview field to responses for enterprise customers so SDKs can show an estimated final token count including server injections. filed infra ticket INFRA-879.

nate (eng): created SDK issue SDK-563 to add include_server_injected flag and expose metering_preview when available. Will work with infra on API semantics.

ryan (customer): appreciated. For INV-1192 can you add a short note on the invoice explaining "server-injected system content and tool output"? That will help our finance team.

tara (support): yes — I'll attach an explanatory note and mark this invoice as reviewed. closing the escalation for now but leaving threads open until SDK/infra mitigation lands. :white_check_mark:

nate (eng): tl;dr root cause = server-side injected system message + plugin/tool output that the client estimator doesn't account for. action items: SDK-563 (estimator opt-in), INFRA-879 (metering preview), support note added to INV-1192.

ryan (customer): thanks all. small ask: can you email me when opt-out flag is live?

tara (support): will do.

billing-bot: invoice INV-1192 flagged: support-reviewed — note added.

nate (eng): reassigning SDK-563 to @nate, will sync with infra tomorrow.

end of thread
